Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

1	# frame-codec
2	
3	Binary frame codec for a length-prefixed wire format, with a checksum, a version byte and precise errors for truncated or damaged input.
4	
5	## Requirements
6	
7	Go 1.22 or newer. Standard library only.
8	
9	## Build
10	
11	    go build ./...
12	    go run ./cmd/framedecode --file <path>
13	
14	## Public interface
15	
16	`codec.Encode(frame Frame) ([]byte, error)` returns the framed bytes.
17	- `codec.Decode(data []byte) (Frame, error)` returns the decoded frame.
18	- `type Frame struct { Version uint8; Flags uint16; Kind uint8; Payload []byte }`.
19	- `codec.HeaderSize`, `codec.MaxPayload` constants.
20	- `codec.ErrShortFrame`, `codec.ErrBadVersion`, `codec.ErrChecksum`, `codec.ErrTooLarge` error values.
21	
22	## Multi-frame sessions
23	
24	`codec.NewSession(w io.Writer, r io.Reader) *Session` wraps one byte
25	writer and one byte reader in a concurrency-safe session. Frames are
26	just concatenated single-frame encodings, so the wire format and the
27	single-frame entries are unchanged.
28	
29	- `(*Session).WriteFrame(Frame) error` appends one whole encoded frame
30	  in call-arrival order; an oversized payload returns `ErrTooLarge`
31	  before any byte is buffered.
32	- `(*Session).Flush() error` writes everything buffered so far to the
33	  underlying writer (and flushes it when it implements `Flush` itself).
34	- `(*Session).ReadFrame() (Frame, error)` parses incrementally: complete
35	  frames are returned one per call while a trailing half frame stays
36	  buffered for later bytes. A clean end of input returns `io.EOF`; a
37	  truncated trailing frame returns `ErrShortFrame`; a corrupt frame
38	  returns the same value `Decode` would return for it and stops further
39	  delivery, with previously returned frames already in the caller's
40	  hands.
41	
42	Reads and writes are independently serialized, so one session may be
43	shared by concurrent writers and readers; the bytes of a single frame
44	are never interleaved.
45	
46	## Reliable sessions
47	
48	`codec.NewReliable(sess *Session, cfg ReliableConfig) (*ReliableSession, error)`
49	wraps an existing session in a reliability layer. The lower wire format
50	is not changed: every reliable message is the payload of one ordinary
51	codec frame, prefixed by this layer's own envelope, so `Encode`/`Decode`,
52	the header constants and the four established error values keep their
53	exact byte-level semantics.
54	
55	- `ReliableConfig{Window int; StateDir string}`: send/receive window
56	  width in frames and a directory for write-side state (checkpoint and
57	  replay log); it is created if missing.
58	- `ReliableFrame{Flags uint16; Kind uint8; Payload []byte}` is the
59	  caller-visible frame. `EnvelopeSize` (16) bytes are reserved inside
60	  the underlying frame, so the inner payload limit is
61	  `ReliableMaxPayload = MaxPayload - EnvelopeSize`.
62	- `(*ReliableSession).WriteFrame(ReliableFrame) error` numbers frames in
63	  write order, journals each one, and parks it in the send window;
64	  nothing goes out before `Flush`. When the window is full it returns
65	  the established over-limit value `ErrWindowFull` (the same sentinel as
66	  `ErrTooLarge`) and drops the frame without consuming a sequence. An
67	  oversized inner payload returns `ErrTooLarge`.
68	- `(*ReliableSession).Flush() error` sends all windowed frames in seq
69	  order, each piggybacking a cumulative "next expected" acknowledgement,
70	  plus one pure ack; on a restart the window is reloaded from the replay
71	  log, so `Flush` is also the retransmit operation.
72	- `(*ReliableSession).ReadFrame() (ReliableFrame, error)` delivers in seq
73	  order exactly once. Acks advance the send window; duplicates of
74	  delivered or parked frames are re-acknowledged but never redelivered;
75	  in-window out-of-order frames are parked and delivered as a contiguous
76	  run once the gap closes; a declared sequence outside the window's
77	  reach (an ancient residual older than one window width, or one width
78	  ahead of the current position) is refused with `ErrChecksum`, stopping
79	  delivery stickily at the current position. Outer-layer results
80	  (`io.EOF`, `ErrShortFrame`, outer checksum/version/size errors) pass
81	  through unchanged.
82	
83	Standalone acks are written by a small background pump, so a writer
84	that needs the peer's acks to drain its window must let `ReadFrame` run
85	(or run it in a dedicated goroutine for one-directional traffic).
86	
87	### Crash recovery
88	
89	Written data frames are recorded in a CRC'd replay log (`reliable.log`);
90	the acknowledged position is recorded in a dual-slot checkpoint
91	(`reliable.ckp`), writing the alternate slot with a higher generation
92	each time:
93	
94	- a checkpoint torn by a crash mid-write fails its own CRC and is
95	  ignored, falling back to the previous complete record;
96	- a truncated replay log, or a flipped bit in a complete record, fails
97	  recovery with `ErrChecksum` rather than delivering unverified frames;
98	- the checkpoint is made durable before the log prefix is discarded, so
99	  reconciliation always resumes from the earlier confirmed position: no
100	  acknowledged frame is resent past the peer's state, no unacknowledged
101	  frame is skipped, and the receiver deduplicates the overlap.
102	
103	After recovery the first `Flush` re-sends every frame past the resume
104	point; backlogs wider than the window drain as acks refill the freed
105	tail slots from the log.
106	
107	## Channel multiplexing
108	
109	`codec.NewMux(rel *ReliableSession, cfg MuxConfig) (*Mux, error)`
110	carries several independent logical channels over one reliable
111	session. The lower wire format is not changed: every multiplexed
112	message is the payload of one reliable data frame, prefixed by this
113	layer's own 15-byte header
114	(`chan uint16`, `seq uint32`, `flags uint8`, `ack uint32`, `crc32`),
115	so the reliable envelope, the codec frame, the header constants and
116	all established error values keep their exact semantics.
117	
118	- `MuxConfig{Channels int; Window int; StateDir string}`: the number of
119	  channels (numbered `0..Channels-1`), the per-channel in-flight quota
120	  in frames (enforced independently), and a write-side state directory
121	  (per-channel dual-slot checkpoints, a shared replay journal and
122	  per-channel close markers), created if missing.
123	- `ChannelFrame{Channel uint16; Flags uint16; Kind uint8; Payload []byte}`
124	  is the caller-visible frame. `MuxHeaderSize` (15) bytes are reserved
125	  inside the reliable payload, so the inner payload limit is
126	  `MuxMaxPayload = ReliableMaxPayload - MuxHeaderSize`.
127	- `(*Mux).WriteFrame(ChannelFrame) error` numbers frames per channel in
128	  write order, journals each one and parks it in the channel's quota;
129	  nothing goes out before `Flush`. A full per-channel quota returns the
130	  established over-limit sentinel `ErrWindowFull` (the same value as
131	  `ErrTooLarge`); an oversized payload returns `ErrTooLarge`. A rejected
132	  frame is neither queued nor journaled and consumes no sequence, so it
133	  takes no quota; total buffering is bounded by `Channels*Window`.
134	  Writing to a closed channel returns the new sentinel
135	  `ErrChannelClosed`; an out-of-range channel returns `ErrChecksum`.
136	- `(*Mux).CloseChannel(ch) error` closes one channel's write side: the
137	  FIN is itself a sequence entry (it takes one quota slot, so a full
138	  quota gives `ErrWindowFull` and the close is retried after acks); a
139	  channel that was never written is opened first, so an unused channel
140	  still delivers a clean EOF. Closing or writing an already closed
141	  channel returns `ErrChannelClosed`.
142	- `(*Mux).Flush() error` sends queued frames round-robin across
143	  channels (each pass serves at most one queued frame per channel,
144	  starting where the previous Flush stopped), so one busy channel can
145	  never starve another and a channel's frames never pass its own
146	  earlier frames. Every frame piggybacks the sender's current
147	  cumulative receive position for its channel; cumulative
148	  acknowledgements are also sent by a small background pump. As on the
149	  reliable layer, a writer that needs the peer's acks to drain quotas
150	  must let `ReadFrame` run.
151	- `(*Mux).ReadFrame() (ChannelFrame, error)` delivers across all
152	  channels: a gap-blocked channel never stalls another channel, while
153	  within a channel frames arrive in write order exactly once. After a
154	  channel's remaining frames, the read that reaches its FIN returns the
155	  `ChannelFrame` naming the channel together with `io.EOF`; other
156	  channels keep flowing. A channel number outside the session's reach,
157	  a residual older than one channel-window, a declaration more than one
158	  window ahead, an acknowledgement past the send frontier, a
159	  same-sequence retransmission with different content, an unknown flag,
160	  an ack carrying payload, or a damaged header is refused with
161	  `ErrChecksum`, stopping stickily at the current delivery positions.
162	  Reliable-layer results (`io.EOF`, `ErrShortFrame`, outer
163	  checksum/version/size and reader errors) pass through unchanged; when
164	  a terminal lower-layer read also brings complete frames, the buffered
165	  frames are delivered first.
166	
167	Restart uses the same durable rules as the reliable layer: written data
168	frames are CRC-recorded in a shared journal (`mux.log`), acknowledged
169	per-channel positions in dual-slot checkpoints (`muxNNN.ckp`), and a
170	close marker (`muxNNN.closed`) survives a FIN whose journal prefix was
171	discarded. Recovery resumes each channel at the earlier of the
172	checkpoint and journal positions, so no unacknowledged frame is skipped
173	and the receiver deduplicates the overlap; a truncated journal or a
174	flipped bit in a complete record fails recovery with `ErrChecksum`.
175	
176	## Tests
177	
178	    go test ./...
179	
180	## Limits
181	
182	Single frame in memory; no streaming reader in this scope.
183	No compression and no encryption.
184	Standard library only.

- `ReliableFrame{Flags uint16; Kind uint8; Payload []byte}` is the

- `(*ReliableSession).WriteFrame(ReliableFrame) error` numbers frames in
  write order, journals each one, and parks it in the send window;
  nothing goes out before `Flush`. When the window is full it returns
  the established over-limit value `ErrWindowFull` (the same sentinel as
  `ErrTooLarge`) and drops the frame without consuming a sequence. An
  oversized inner payload returns `ErrTooLarge`.
- `(*ReliableSession).Flush() error` sends all windowed frames in seq
  order, each piggybacking a cumulative "next expected" acknowledgement,
  plus one pure ack; on a restart the window is reloaded from the replay
  log, so `Flush` is also the retransmit operation.
- `(*ReliableSession).ReadFrame() (ReliableFrame, error)` delivers in seq
  order exactly once. Acks advance the send window; duplicates of
  delivered or parked frames are re-acknowledged but never redelivered;
  in-window out-of-order frames are parked and delivered as a contiguous
  run once the gap closes; a declared sequence outside the window's
  reach (an ancient residual older than one window width, or one width
  ahead of the current position) is refused with `ErrChecksum`, stopping
  delivery stickily at the current position. Outer-layer results
  (`io.EOF`, `ErrShortFrame`, outer checksum/version/size errors) pass
  through unchanged.

Standalone acks are written by a small background pump, so a writer
that needs the peer's acks to drain its window must let `ReadFrame` run
(or run it in a dedicated goroutine for one-directional traffic).

### Crash recovery

Written data frames are recorded in a CRC'd replay log (`reliable.log`);
the acknowledged position is recorded in a dual-slot checkpoint
(`reliable.ckp`), writing the alternate slot with a higher generation
each time:

- a checkpoint torn by a crash mid-write fails its own CRC and is
  ignored, falling back to the previous complete record;
- a truncated replay log, or a flipped bit in a complete record, fails
  recovery with `ErrChecksum` rather than delivering unverified frames;
- the checkpoint is made durable before the log prefix is discarded, so
  reconciliation always resumes from the earlier confirmed position: no
  acknowledged frame is resent past the peer's state, no unacknowledged
  frame is skipped, and the receiver deduplicates the overlap.

After recovery the first `Flush` re-sends every frame past the resume
point; backlogs wider than the window drain as acks refill the freed
tail slots from the log.

## Channel multiplexing

`codec.NewMux(rel *ReliableSession, cfg MuxConfig) (*Mux, error)`
carries several independent logical channels over one reliable
session. The lower wire format is not changed: every multiplexed
message is the payload of one reliable data frame, prefixed by this
layer's own 15-byte header
(`chan uint16`, `seq uint32`, `flags uint8`, `ack uint32`, `crc32`),
so the reliable envelope, the codec frame, the header constants and
all established error values keep their exact semantics.

- `MuxConfig{Channels int; Window int; StateDir string}`: the number of
  channels (numbered `0..Channels-1`), the per-channel in-flight quota
  in frames (enforced independently), and a write-side state directory
  (per-channel dual-slot checkpoints, a shared replay journal and
  per-channel close markers), created if missing.
- `ChannelFrame{Channel uint16; Flags uint16; Kind uint8; Payload []byte}`
  is the caller-visible frame. `MuxHeaderSize` (15) bytes are reserved
  inside the reliable payload, so the inner payload limit is
  `MuxMaxPayload = ReliableMaxPayload - MuxHeaderSize`.
- `(*Mux).WriteFrame(ChannelFrame) error` numbers frames per channel in
  write order, journals each one and parks it in the channel's quota;
  nothing goes out before `Flush`. A full per-channel quota returns the
  established over-limit sentinel `ErrWindowFull` (the same value as
  `ErrTooLarge`); an oversized payload returns `ErrTooLarge`. A rejected
  frame is neither queued nor journaled and consumes no sequence, so it
  takes no quota; total buffering is bounded by `Channels*Window`.
  Writing to a closed channel returns the new sentinel
  `ErrChannelClosed`; an out-of-range channel returns `ErrChecksum`.
- `(*Mux).CloseChannel(ch) error` closes one channel's write side: the
  FIN is itself a sequence entry (it takes one quota slot, so a full
  quota gives `ErrWindowFull` and the close is retried after acks); a
  channel that was never written is opened first, so an unused channel
  still delivers a clean EOF. Closing or writing an already closed
  channel returns `ErrChannelClosed`.
- `(*Mux).Flush() error` sends queued frames round-robin across
  channels (each pass serves at most one queued frame per channel,
  starting where the previous Flush stopped), so one busy channel can
  never starve another and a channel's frames never pass its own
  earlier frames. Every frame piggybacks the sender's current
  cumulative receive position for its channel; cumulative
  acknowledgements are also sent by a small background pump. As on the
  reliable layer, a writer that needs the peer's acks to drain quotas
  must let `ReadFrame` run.
- `(*Mux).ReadFrame() (ChannelFrame, error)` delivers across all
  channels: a gap-blocked channel never stalls another channel, while
  within a channel frames arrive in write order exactly once. After a
  channel's remaining frames, the read that reaches its FIN returns the
  `ChannelFrame` naming the channel together with `io.EOF`; other
  channels keep flowing. A channel number outside the session's reach,
  a residual older than one channel-window, a declaration more than one
  window ahead, an acknowledgement past the send frontier, a
  same-sequence retransmission with different content, an unknown flag,
  an ack carrying payload, or a damaged header is refused with
  `ErrChecksum`, stopping stickily at the current delivery positions.
  Reliable-layer results (`io.EOF`, `ErrShortFrame`, outer
  checksum/version/size and reader errors) pass through unchanged; when
  a terminal lower-layer read also brings complete frames, the buffered
  frames are delivered first.

Restart uses the same durable rules as the reliable layer: written data
frames are CRC-recorded in a shared journal (`mux.log`), acknowledged
per-channel positions in dual-slot checkpoints (`muxNNN.ckp`), and a
close marker (`muxNNN.closed`) survives a FIN whose journal prefix was
discarded. Recovery resumes each channel at the earlier of the
checkpoint and journal positions, so no unacknowledged frame is skipped
and the receiver deduplicates the overlap; a truncated journal or a
flipped bit in a complete record fails recovery with `ErrChecksum`.

## Tests

    go test ./...

## Limits

Single frame in memory; no streaming reader in this scope.
No compression and no encryption.
Standard library only.

426	// Flush sends every queued frame with transmission opportunities handed
427	// out round-robin across channels: starting where the previous Flush
428	// stopped, each pass takes at most one queued frame per channel, so a
429	// continuously busy channel can never starve the others and frames
430	// never overtake an earlier frame of their own channel. Every data
431	// frame piggybacks the sender's current receive position for its
432	// channel; standalone acks for every channel follow the run.
433	//
434	// After a restart the queue was reloaded from the journal, so Flush is
435	// also the retransmit operation; the receiver deduplicates overlaps.
436	func (m *Mux) Flush() error {
437		// Snapshot receive positions BEFORE taking the send lock: the read
438		// path takes mu while applying acks (rmu-then-mu order), so mu must
439		// never be held while taking rmu.
440		m.rmu.Lock()
441		acks := make([]uint32, m.cfg.Channels)
442		copy(acks, m.bases)
443		m.rmu.Unlock()
444	
445		m.mu.Lock()
446		out := m.buildFlushLocked(acks)
447		m.mu.Unlock()
448	
449		// Hand the planned run to the reliable session in round-robin
450		// order. Its own window can fill (a restart backlog wider than one
451		// window, or a slow peer): that is backpressure, not an error. Stop
452		// there, flush the accepted prefix and leave every unhanded frame
453		// queued for the next Flush; the receiver deduplicates the overlap.
454		lastServed := -1
455		for i := range out {
456			err := m.rel.WriteFrame(out[i])
457			if errors.Is(err, ErrWindowFull) {
458				break
459			}
460			if err != nil {
461				return err
462			}
463			// out is one data frame per queued entry; recover its channel
464			// from its mux header rather than re-planning.
465			lastServed = int(binary.BigEndian.Uint16(out[i].Payload[mhChanOff:mhSeqOff]))
466		}
467		if err := m.rel.Flush(); err != nil {
468			return err
469		}
470	
471		// Advance the round-robin cursor only past channels that actually
472		// got a frame onto the wire this Flush, and only after the lower
473		// flush succeeded: a failed Flush retries from the same channel.
474		if lastServed >= 0 {
475			m.mu.Lock()
476			m.rr = (lastServed + 1) % m.cfg.Channels
477			m.mu.Unlock()
478		}
479		return nil
480	}
481	
482	// buildFlushLocked returns the data frames of one Flush in wire order.
483	// It never mutates the queue or the round-robin cursor. The caller
484	// holds mu.
485	func (m *Mux) buildFlushLocked(acks []uint32) []ReliableFrame {
486		// Entries of one channel are always in ascending seq order (append
487		// order at write time, journal order after a restart); pending just
488		// tracks which have been taken during this Flush.
489		pending := make([]*queuedFrame, len(m.queue))
490		copy(pending, m.queue)
491	
492		out := make([]ReliableFrame, 0, len(pending))
493		cursor := m.rr
494		for len(pending) > 0 {
495			startCh := cursor
496			taken := false
497			for step := 0; step < m.cfg.Channels; step++ {
498				ch := uint16((startCh + step) % m.cfg.Channels)
499				// The peer accepts exactly this channel's next Window
500				// sequences; frames past the reach wait for an ack, so a
501				// restart backlog wider than one window drains gradually
502				// instead of being refused as "too far ahead".
503				reach := m.sc[ch].acked + uint32(m.cfg.Window)
504				idx := -1
505				for i, qf := range pending {
506					if qf.channel != ch {
507						continue
508					}
509					if qf.seq >= reach {
510						break // per-channel entries are ascending
511					}
512					idx = i
513					break
514				}
515				if idx < 0 {
516					continue
517				}
518				qf := pending[idx]
519				pending = append(pending[:idx], pending[idx+1:]...)
520				flag := uint8(0)
521				if qf.fin {
522					flag = mhFlagFin
523				}
524				out = append(out, ReliableFrame{
525					Flags:   qf.flags,
526					Kind:    qf.kind,
527					Payload: encodeMuxHeader(qf.channel, qf.seq, flag, acks[qf.channel], qf.payload),
528				})
529				taken = true
530				cursor = int(ch) + 1 // next pass starts after the served channel
531			}
532			if !taken {
533				break
534			}
535		}
536		return out
537	}
538	
539	// ReadFrame returns the next deliverable frame across all channels.
540	// Channels are scanned independently: a channel parked waiting for a
541	// gap is skipped, so it never stalls another channel. Within a channel
542	// frames arrive in write order exactly once; out-of-order frames are
543	// parked until their gap closes.
544	//
545	// When a channel's FIN is reached - after every earlier frame of that
546	// channel was delivered - the call returns io.EOF together with a
547	// ChannelFrame whose Channel names the closed channel; reads on other
548	// channels continue unaffected.
549	//
550	// The following are refused with the established ErrChecksum and stop
551	// delivery stickily at the current positions: a channel number outside
552	// the session's reach, a residual frame older than one channel-window,
553	// a frame more than one channel-window ahead, an acknowledgement past
554	// the send frontier, a same-sequence retransmission with different
555	// content, an unknown flag, an ack frame carrying payload, and a
556	// damaged mux header. Reliable-layer results (the transport's io.EOF,
557	// ErrShortFrame, outer checksum/version/size and reader errors) pass
558	// through unchanged, and complete frames already buffered are delivered
559	// before a terminal lower-layer result is surfaced.
560	func (m *Mux) ReadFrame() (ChannelFrame, error) {
561		for {
562			m.rmu.Lock()
563			if m.rerr != nil {
564				err := m.rerr
565				m.rmu.Unlock()
566				return ChannelFrame{}, err
567			}
568			if cf, eof, ok := m.nextDeliverableLocked(); ok {
569				m.rmu.Unlock()
570				if eof {
571					return cf, io.EOF
572				}
573				return cf, nil
574			}
575			m.rmu.Unlock()
576	
577			// Block in the reliable reader WITHOUT holding rmu, exactly like
578			// the layer below: sends and ack processing must keep moving
579			// while this waits for bytes.
580			outer, rerr := m.rel.ReadFrame()
581	
582			m.rmu.Lock()
583			if m.rerr != nil {
584				err := m.rerr
585				m.rmu.Unlock()
586				return ChannelFrame{}, err
587			}
588			if rerr != nil {
589				// The lower layer hands over its terminal result together
590				// with any bytes that arrived in the same read; complete
591				// frames already parsed below are parked in held. Deliver
592				// every buffered frame across all channels first, and only
593				// surface the terminal result once the buffer is drained;
594				// the result is sticky and returns again on later calls.
595				if cf, eof, ok := m.nextDeliverableLocked(); ok {
596					m.rmu.Unlock()
597					if eof {
598						return cf, io.EOF
599					}
600					return cf, nil
601				}
602				return m.failReadLocked(rerr)
603			}
604	
605			ch, seq, flag, ack, payload, err := decodeMuxHeader(outer.Payload)
606			if err != nil {
607				return m.failReadLocked(err)
608			}
609			if int(ch) >= m.cfg.Channels {
610				return m.failReadLocked(fmt.Errorf(
611					"codec: mux channel %d out of range [0,%d): %w",
612					ch, m.cfg.Channels, ErrChecksum))
613			}
614			if flag&^uint8(mhFlagFin|mhFlagAck) != 0 {
615				return m.failReadLocked(fmt.Errorf(
616					"codec: mux ch %d seq %d unknown flags %#x: %w",
617					ch, seq, flag, ErrChecksum))
618			}
619			isAck := flag&mhFlagAck != 0
620			isFin := flag&mhFlagFin != 0
621			if isAck && (isFin || seq != 0 || len(payload) != 0) {
622				return m.failReadLocked(fmt.Errorf(
623					"codec: mux ch %d malformed ack frame (fin=%v seq=%d payload=%d): %w",
624					ch, isFin, seq, len(payload), ErrChecksum))
625			}
626			if isFin && len(payload) != 0 {
627				return m.failReadLocked(fmt.Errorf(
628					"codec: mux ch %d FIN seq %d carries %d payload bytes: %w",
629					ch, seq, len(payload), ErrChecksum))
630			}
631	
632			// Every inbound message states a cumulative position for its
633			// channel; one past anything this side ever sent is impossible
634			// in a well-behaved stream and is refused before anything is
635			// parked or delivered.
636			m.mu.Lock()
637			overFrontier := ack > m.sc[ch].next
638			frontier := m.sc[ch].next
639			m.mu.Unlock()
640			if overFrontier {
641				return m.failReadLocked(fmt.Errorf(
642					"codec: mux ch %d ack %d past send frontier %d: %w",
643					ch, ack, frontier, ErrChecksum))
644			}
645			m.applyAck(ch, ack)
646	
647			if isAck {
648				m.rmu.Unlock()
649				continue
650			}
651	
652			cf := ChannelFrame{Channel: ch, Flags: outer.Flags, Kind: outer.Kind, Payload: payload}
653			fr := inboundFrame{cf: cf, fin: isFin}
654			key := muxSeq{ch: ch, seq: seq}
655			base := m.bases[ch]
656	
657			switch classify(seq, base, m.cfg.Window) {
658			case seqInWindow:
659				// A closed channel never carries another NEW sequence: its
660				// FIN was the stream's last entry. Duplicate retransmits
661				// (below the base) fall through to seqDuplicate and are
662				// matched against the first delivered copy.
663				if m.finEOF[ch] {
664					return m.failReadLocked(fmt.Errorf(
665						"codec: mux ch %d received new frame seq %d after FIN at %d: %w",
666						ch, seq, base, ErrChecksum))
667				}
668				if prev, dup := m.held[key]; dup {
669					// A retransmission of a parked frame must describe the
670					// same frame. A same-sequence conflict is refused
671					// instead of guessed, and delivery stops here.
672					if !sameInbound(prev, fr) {
673						return m.failReadLocked(fmt.Errorf(
674							"codec: mux ch %d seq %d retransmission conflicts: %w",
675							ch, seq, ErrChecksum))
676					}
677				} else if prev, seen := m.seen[key]; seen {
678					// Already delivered once: any conflicting second
679					// declaration of the same sequence is a protocol error.
680					if !sameInbound(prev, fr) {
681						return m.failReadLocked(fmt.Errorf(
682							"codec: mux ch %d seq %d duplicate conflicts with delivered frame: %w",
683							ch, seq, ErrChecksum))
684					}
685				} else {
686					m.held[key] = fr
687				}
688				// Restate the channel's cumulative position either way so a
689				// lost acknowledgement does not make the peer resend
690				// forever.
691				m.signalAckLocked(ch)
692				m.rmu.Unlock()
693				continue // deliver held[base] from the top of the loop
694			case seqDuplicate:
695				// Behind the base but within one window width. Compare with
696				// the first copy delivered for that sequence; an
697				// irreconcilable retransmission is refused.
698				prev, known := m.seen[key]
699				if known && !sameInbound(prev, fr) {
700					return m.failReadLocked(fmt.Errorf(
701						"codec: mux ch %d seq %d duplicate conflicts with delivered frame: %w",
702						ch, seq, ErrChecksum))
703				}
704				m.signalAckLocked(ch)
705				m.rmu.Unlock()
706				continue
707			default: // seqStale
708				return m.failReadLocked(fmt.Errorf(
709					"codec: mux ch %d seq %d outside window at %d (width %d): %w",
710					ch, seq, base, m.cfg.Window, ErrChecksum))
711			}
712		}
713	}
714	
715	// sameInbound reports whether two arrivals claiming one sequence carry
716	// the same frame (FIN marking, flags, kind and payload).
717	func sameInbound(a, b inboundFrame) bool {
718		if a.fin != b.fin {
719			return false
720		}
721		if a.fin {
722			return true // FIN entries carry no caller frame
723		}
724		return a.cf.Flags == b.cf.Flags && a.cf.Kind == b.cf.Kind &&
725			bytes.Equal(a.cf.Payload, b.cf.Payload)
726	}
727	
728	// nextDeliverableLocked finds the lowest-numbered channel whose due
729	// sequence is parked (a FIN-closed channel is skipped), records the
730	// delivery and asks for an acknowledgement. It returns eof=true when
731	// the delivered entry is the channel's FIN: the caller then returns
732	// (ChannelFrame{Channel: ch}, io.EOF). Caller holds rmu.
733	func (m *Mux) nextDeliverableLocked() (cf ChannelFrame, eof bool, ok bool) {
734		for ch := 0; ch < m.cfg.Channels; ch++ {
735			if m.finEOF[ch] {
736				continue
737			}
738			key := muxSeq{ch: uint16(ch), seq: m.bases[ch]}
739			fr, present := m.held[key]
740			if !present {
741				continue
742			}
743			delete(m.held, key)
744			m.bases[ch] = key.seq + 1
745	
746			// Remember the delivered frame for conflict checks on its
747			// duplicates. Exactly one sequence falls out of the duplicate
748			// span per one-step advance (the span ends one window width
749			// behind the base), so the seen table stays bounded by
750			// Channels*Window with an O(1) prune.
751			m.seen[key] = fr
752			delete(m.seen, muxSeq{ch: key.ch, seq: key.seq - uint32(m.cfg.Window)})
753	
754			m.signalAckLocked(key.ch)
755			if fr.fin {
756				m.finEOF[ch] = true
757				return ChannelFrame{Channel: key.ch}, true, true
758			}
759			return fr.cf, false, true
760		}
761		return ChannelFrame{}, false, false
762	}
763	
764	// applyAck advances one channel's cumulative send position, releases
765	// the freed quota slots and discards the journal prefix once the new
766	// position is durable. Positions that do not move the channel forward
767	// are ignored. The caller holds rmu (rmu-then-mu order).
768	func (m *Mux) applyAck(ch uint16, ack uint32) {
769		m.mu.Lock()
770		defer m.mu.Unlock()
771	
772		c := &m.sc[ch]
773		if ack <= c.acked || ack > c.next {
774			return
775		}
776	
777		kept := m.queue[:0]
778		for _, qf := range m.queue {
779			if qf.channel == ch && qf.seq < ack {
780				continue
781			}
782			kept = append(kept, qf)
783		}
784		m.queue = kept
785		c.acked = ack
786	
787		// Durable per-channel position BEFORE the journal prefix is
788		// discarded: a crash between the two only leaves extra frames to
789		// dedupe, never a gap.
790		if err := saveMuxCheckpoint(m.cfg.StateDir, ch, ack); err == nil && m.log != nil {
791			_ = m.log.prefix(m.sc)
792		}
793	}
794	
795	// signalAckLocked coalescingly asks the background sender to restate
796	// the channel's cumulative position. It never blocks. Caller holds rmu.
797	func (m *Mux) signalAckLocked(ch uint16) {
798		select {
799		case m.standCh <- standAck{ch: ch, next: m.bases[ch]}:
800		default:
801		}
802	}
803	
804	// pumpAck serializes standalone acknowledgement writes so they happen on
805	// this goroutine, never on a reader's: two peers reading at once cannot
806	// block each other. Every wakeup drains the whole queue and sends at
807	// most one cumulative ack per channel stating its latest position, so a
808	// burst of deliveries or duplicate retransmits costs a handful of
809	// frames rather than one per arrival.
810	func (m *Mux) pumpAck() {
811		defer close(m.doneCh)
812		for {
813			select {
814			case <-m.stopCh:
815				return
816			case first := <-m.standCh:
817				latest := map[uint16]uint32{first.ch: first.next}
818				draining := true
819				for draining {
820					select {
821					case a := <-m.standCh:
822						if a.next >= latest[a.ch] {
823							latest[a.ch] = a.next
824						}
825					default:
826						draining = false
827					}
828				}
829				// Send in channel order for deterministic wire output.
830				for ch := 0; ch < m.cfg.Channels; ch++ {
831					next, ok := latest[uint16(ch)]
832					if !ok {
833						continue
834					}
835					b := encodeMuxHeader(uint16(ch), 0, mhFlagAck, next, nil)
836					if err := m.rel.WriteFrame(ReliableFrame{Payload: b}); err == nil {
837						_ = m.rel.Flush()
838					}
839				}
840			}
841		}
842	}

844	// failReadLocked records the terminal read-side result, releases rmu and
845	// returns it. Every caller returns immediately after calling it.
846	func (m *Mux) failReadLocked(err error) (ChannelFrame, error) {
847		m.rerr = err
848		m.rmu.Unlock()
849		return ChannelFrame{}, err
850	}

852	// Close stops the background acknowledgement sender. Fully journaled
853	// but unacknowledged frames remain in the mux journal for a later
854	// restart to resend.
855	func (m *Mux) Close() error {
856		m.closeOnce.Do(func() { close(m.stopCh) })
857		return nil

860	// ----------------------------------------------------------------------
861	// Mux header encoding.
862	// ----------------------------------------------------------------------
863	
864	// encodeMuxHeader serializes one mux message into reliable payload
865	// bytes.
866	func encodeMuxHeader(ch uint16, seq uint32, flags uint8, ack uint32, payload []byte) []byte {
867		out := make([]byte, MuxHeaderSize+len(payload))
868		binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(out[mhChanOff:mhSeqOff], ch)
869		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[mhSeqOff:mhFlagOff], seq)
870		out[mhFlagOff] = flags
871		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[mhAckOff:mhCRCOff], ack)
872		copy(out[mhBodyOff:], payload)
873		h := crc32.NewIEEE()
874		h.Write(out[:mhCRCOff])
875		h.Write(out[mhBodyOff:])
876		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[mhCRCOff:mhBodyOff], h.Sum32())
877		return out
878	}
879	
880	// decodeMuxHeader parses one mux message. A message too short for the
881	// fixed header is reported with ErrShortFrame; a damaged header or
882	// payload with ErrChecksum.
883	func decodeMuxHeader(p []byte) (ch uint16, seq uint32, flags uint8, ack uint32, payload []byte, err error) {
884		if len(p) < MuxHeaderSize {
885			return 0, 0, 0, 0, nil, ErrShortFrame
886		}
887		h := crc32.NewIEEE()
888		h.Write(p[:mhCRCOff])
889		h.Write(p[mhBodyOff:])
890		if h.Sum32() != binary.BigEndian.Uint32(p[mhCRCOff:mhBodyOff]) {
891			return 0, 0, 0, 0, nil, ErrChecksum
892		}
893		ch = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(p[mhChanOff:mhSeqOff])
894		seq = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(p[mhSeqOff:mhFlagOff])
895		flags = p[mhFlagOff]
896		ack = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(p[mhAckOff:mhCRCOff])
897		body := make([]byte, len(p)-MuxHeaderSize)
898		copy(body, p[mhBodyOff:])
899		return ch, seq, flags, ack, body, nil
900	}

903	// Durable state: one dual-slot, checksummed checkpoint file per channel
904	// and one strict CRC'd replay journal shared by all channels.

908		muxCheckpointPrefix = "mux"
909		muxCheckpointSuffix = ".ckp"
910		muxJournalName      = "mux.log"

912		muxCPRecordSize = 4 + 4 + 4 // generation + ack + crc32
913		muxCPSlotSize   = 2 * muxCPRecordSize
914	
915		// ch(2) + seq(4) + fin(1) + flags(2) + kind(1) + len(4) + crc(4).

960	// markMuxChannelClosed durably records that ch's write side is closed.
961	func markMuxChannelClosed(dir string, ch uint16) error {
962		f, err := os.OpenFile(muxClosePath(dir, ch), os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREATE|os.O_TRUNC, 0o644)
963		if err != nil {
964			return err
965		}
966		if _, err := f.Write([]byte("closed\n")); err != nil {
967			f.Close()
968			return err
969		}
970		if err := f.Sync(); err != nil {

972			return err
973		}

977	// muxChannelClosed reports whether the durable close marker exists.
978	func muxChannelClosed(dir string, ch uint16) (bool, error) {
979		switch _, err := os.Stat(muxClosePath(dir, ch)); {
980		case err == nil:
981			return true, nil
982		case os.IsNotExist(err):
983			return false, nil
984		default:
985			return false, err
986		}

989	// loadMuxCheckpoint returns a channel's newest valid checkpointed
990	// "next expected" position. Missing state, an empty file or records
991	// that all fail validation mean position 0: with nothing confirmed the
992	// safe action is to replay what the journal holds and let the receiver
993	// deduplicate the overlap.
994	func loadMuxCheckpoint(dir string, ch uint16) (uint32, error) {
995		data, err := os.ReadFile(muxCheckpointPath(dir, ch))
996		if err != nil {
997			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
998				return 0, nil
999			}
1000			return 0, err
1001		}
1002		var bestGen, bestAck uint32
1003		found := false
1004		for off := 0; off+muxCPRecordSize <= len(data); off += muxCPRecordSize {
1005			if binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[off+8:off+12]) != crc32.ChecksumIEEE(data[off:off+8]) {
1006				continue
1007			}
1008			gen := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[off : off+4])
1009			ack := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[off+4 : off+8])
1010			if !found || gen > bestGen || (gen == bestGen && ack > bestAck) {
1011				bestGen, bestAck, found = gen, ack, true
1012			}
1013		}
1014		if !found {
1015			return 0, nil
1016		}
1017		return bestAck, nil
1018	}
1019	
1020	// nextMuxCPSlot chooses the slot to overwrite and the next generation:
1021	// alternate slots, strictly increasing generations.
1022	func nextMuxCPSlot(dir string, ch uint16) (slot int, generation uint32, err error) {
1023		data, rerr := os.ReadFile(muxCheckpointPath(dir, ch))
1024		if rerr != nil && !os.IsNotExist(rerr) {
1025			return 0, 0, rerr
1026		}
1027		var gens [2]uint32
1028		var ok [2]bool
1029		for i := 0; i < 2; i++ {
1030			lo, hi := i*muxCPRecordSize, (i+1)*muxCPRecordSize
1031			if len(data) >= hi &&
1032				binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[lo+8:lo+12]) == crc32.ChecksumIEEE(data[lo:lo+8]) {
1033				gens[i], ok[i] = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[lo:lo+4]), true
1034			}
1035		}
1036		switch {
1037		case !ok[0] && !ok[1]:
1038			return 0, 1, nil
1039		case ok[0] && (!ok[1] || gens[0] >= gens[1]):
1040			return 1, gens[0] + 1, nil
1041		default:
1042			return 0, gens[1] + 1, nil
1043		}
1044	}
1045	
1046	// saveMuxCheckpoint writes one new record into the alternate slot of
1047	// the channel's checkpoint file, leaving the other slot untouched so at
1048	// least the previous complete record always survives.
1049	func saveMuxCheckpoint(dir string, ch uint16, ack uint32) error {
1050		slot, generation, err := nextMuxCPSlot(dir, ch)
1051		if err != nil {
1052			return err
1053		}
1054		path := muxCheckpointPath(dir, ch)
1055	
1056		needPad := true
1057		if info, statErr := os.Stat(path); statErr == nil && info.Size() >= int64(muxCPSlotSize) {
1058			needPad = false
1059		}
1060		f, err := os.OpenFile(path, os.O_RDWR|os.O_CREATE, 0o644)
1061		if err != nil {
1062			return err
1063		}

1081	func openMuxLog(dir string) (*muxLog, error) {
1082		l := &muxLog{path: filepath.Join(dir, muxJournalName)}
1083		if err := l.load(); err != nil {
1084			return nil, err

1089	func (l *muxLog) load() error {
1090		data, err := os.ReadFile(l.path)
1091		if err != nil {
1092			if os.IsNotExist(err) {
1093				return nil
1094			}
1095			return err
1096		}
1097		for off := 0; off < len(data); {
1098			// Any bytes that do not form a complete, valid record are a
1099			// truncated tail: strict failure, no further delivery.
1100			if len(data)-off < muxLogHdrSize {
1101				return fmt.Errorf("codec: mux journal %s truncated: %w", muxJournalName, ErrChecksum)
1102			}
1103			hdr := data[off : off+muxLogHdrSize]
1104			ch := binary.BigEndian.Uint16(hdr[0:2])
1105			seq := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(hdr[2:6])
1106			fin := hdr[6] != 0
1107			if hdr[6]&^1 != 0 {

1111			kind := hdr[9]

1113			wantCRC := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(hdr[14:18])

1115			if plen < 0 || end > len(data) {

1117			}
1118			h := crc32.NewIEEE()
1119			h.Write(hdr[:14])
1120			h.Write(data[off+muxLogHdrSize : end])
1121			if h.Sum32() != wantCRC {
1122				return fmt.Errorf("codec: mux journal %s corrupted: %w", muxJournalName, ErrChecksum)
1123			}
1124			payload := make([]byte, plen)
1125			copy(payload, data[off+muxLogHdrSize:end])
1126			l.recs = append(l.recs, muxLogRecord{
1127				ch: ch, seq: seq, fin: fin, flags: flags, kind: kind,
1128				f: ChannelFrame{Channel: ch, Flags: flags, Kind: kind, Payload: payload},
1129			})

1131		}
1132		return nil
1133	}

1136	func (l *muxLog) append(qf queuedFrame) error {
1137		l.mu.Lock()
1138		defer l.mu.Unlock()

1140		hdr := make([]byte, muxLogHdrSize)

1154		file, err := os.OpenFile(l.path, os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREATE|os.O_APPEND, 0o644)

1157		}

1161			file.Close()

1163		}

1165			file.Close()
1166			return err
1167		}
1168		if err := file.Close(); err != nil {

1170		}
1171	
1172		l.recs = append(l.recs, muxLogRecord{
1173			ch:    qf.channel,
1174			seq:   qf.seq,
1175			fin:   qf.fin,
1176			flags: qf.flags,
1177			kind:  qf.kind,
1178			f: ChannelFrame{
1179				Channel: qf.channel, Flags: qf.flags, Kind: qf.kind, Payload: qf.payload,
1180			},

1183	}

1188	func (l *muxLog) prefix(sc []sendChannel) error {
1189		l.mu.Lock()
1190		defer l.mu.Unlock()
1191	
1192		keep := l.recs[:0]

1200			return nil
1201		}
1202		l.recs = keep
1203

1205		f, err := os.OpenFile(tmp, os.O_WRONLY|os.O_CREATE|os.O_TRUNC, 0o644)
1206		if err != nil {
1207			return err
1208		}
1209		writeRec := func(r muxLogRecord) error {
1210			hdr := make([]byte, muxLogHdrSize)
1211			binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(hdr[0:2], r.ch)

1217			hdr[9] = r.kind

1219			h := crc32.NewIEEE()

1238		}

1	// Package codec implements encoding and decoding of single binary frames
2	// in a length-prefixed wire format.
3	//
4	// Wire layout (all multi-byte fields big-endian):
5	//
6	//	+------------+---------+--------+------+----------+=========+
7	//	| length (4) | ver (1) | flags(2)| kind(1)| cksum(2) | payload |
8	//	+------------+---------+--------+------+----------+=========+
9	//
10	// The 4-byte length counts payload bytes only. The 10-byte header is
11	// length + version + flags + kind + checksum. The checksum is the low
12	// 16 bits of the byte-wise sum of all header bytes except the checksum
13	// field itself, plus every payload byte.
14	package codec
15	
16	import (
17		"encoding/binary"
18		"errors"
19	)
20	
21	const (
22		// Version is the only protocol version this codec reads and writes.
23		Version = 1
24	
25		// HeaderSize is the total header length in bytes:
26		// 4 (length) + 1 (version) + 2 (flags) + 1 (kind) + 2 (checksum).
27		HeaderSize = 10
28	
29		// MaxPayload is the maximum payload size in bytes a frame may carry.
30		MaxPayload = 1 << 20 // 1 MiB
31	)
32	
33	var (
34		// ErrShortFrame is returned when the input is too short to contain a
35		// complete frame.
36		ErrShortFrame = errors.New("codec: short frame")
37		// ErrBadVersion is returned when the frame version is not supported.
38		ErrBadVersion = errors.New("codec: unsupported version")
39		// ErrChecksum is returned when the checksum does not match the
40		// recomputed value.
41		ErrChecksum = errors.New("codec: checksum mismatch")
42		// ErrTooLarge is returned when the payload exceeds MaxPayload.
43		ErrTooLarge = errors.New("codec: payload too large")
44	)
45	
46	// Frame is a single decoded frame, or the input to Encode.
47	type Frame struct {
48		Version uint8
49		Flags   uint16
50		Kind    uint8
51		Payload []byte
52	}
53	
54	// checksum sums every byte of header-and-payload except the checksum
55	// field itself and keeps the low 16 bits.
56	func checksum(data []byte) uint16 {
57		var sum uint32
58		for _, b := range data {
59			sum += uint32(b)
60		}
61		return uint16(sum)
62	}
63	
64	// Encode serializes f into the wire format. The version written is
65	// always Version. It returns ErrTooLarge if the payload exceeds
66	// MaxPayload.
67	func Encode(f Frame) ([]byte, error) {
68		if len(f.Payload) > MaxPayload {
69			return nil, ErrTooLarge
70		}
71	
72		out := make([]byte, HeaderSize+len(f.Payload))
73		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[0:4], uint32(len(f.Payload)))
74		out[4] = Version
75		binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(out[5:7], f.Flags)
76		out[7] = f.Kind
77		copy(out[HeaderSize:], f.Payload)
78	
79		// Sum the header bytes before the checksum field plus the payload.
80		sum := checksum(out[0:8]) + checksum(out[HeaderSize:])
81		binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(out[8:10], sum)
82		return out, nil
83	}
84	
85	// Decode parses one frame from data. On any error it returns the zero
86	// Frame and one of ErrShortFrame, ErrBadVersion, ErrChecksum or
87	// ErrTooLarge; checks run in that order so the same corrupt input always
88	// yields the same error.
89	func Decode(data []byte) (Frame, error) {
90		var f Frame
91	
92		// 1. Length: enough bytes for the header, then for the declared payload.
93		if len(data) < HeaderSize {
94			return f, ErrShortFrame
95		}
96		payloadLen := binary.BigEndian.Uint32(data[0:4])
97		if uint64(len(data)) < uint64(HeaderSize)+uint64(payloadLen) {
98			return f, ErrShortFrame
99		}
100	
101		// 2. Version.
102		version := data[4]
103		if version != Version {
104			return f, ErrBadVersion
105		}
106	
107		// 3. Checksum over header (minus the checksum field) and payload.
108		want := binary.BigEndian.Uint16(data[8:10])
109		got := checksum(data[0:8]) + checksum(data[HeaderSize:HeaderSize+int(payloadLen)])
110		if got != want {
111			return f, ErrChecksum
112		}
113	
114		// 4. Size.
115		if payloadLen > MaxPayload {
116			return f, ErrTooLarge
117		}
118	
119		payload := make([]byte, payloadLen)
120		copy(payload, data[HeaderSize:HeaderSize+int(payloadLen)])
121	
122		f.Version = version
123		f.Flags = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(data[5:7])
124		f.Kind = data[7]
125		f.Payload = payload
126		return f, nil
127	}

14	// Reliable transport on top of the multi-frame Session.
15	//
16	// This layer adds sequence numbers, cumulative acknowledgements and a
17	// sliding-window pipeline. It does not touch the wire encoding of the
18	// layer below: every reliable message is carried inside the Payload of
19	// one ordinary codec frame, prefixed by this layer's own envelope. The
20	// Encode/Decode entries, the header constants and the four existing
21	// error values keep their exact byte-level semantics.
22	//
23	// Envelope layout inside a codec frame payload (all multi-byte fields
24	// big-endian):
25	//
26	//		+---------+---------+--------+----------+---------+----------+=========+
27	//		| seq (4) | ack (4) | type(1)| flags(2) | kind(1) | crc32(4) | payload |
28	//		+---------+---------+--------+----------+---------+----------+=========+
29	//
30	//	  - seq: sender-assigned data sequence; ACK frames carry no data seq.
31	//	  - ack: cumulative acknowledgement as a "next expected" count: every
32	//	    data frame with seq < ack has been delivered to the reader.
33	//	  - type: 1 = data, 2 = pure acknowledgement.
34	//	  - flags/kind: the caller frame's Flags and Kind, carried inside the
35	//	    envelope; the outer codec Kind is a fixed marker of this layer.
36	//	  - crc32: IEEE CRC of the other 12 envelope bytes plus the payload.
37	//
38	// The underlying frame's payload limit stays MaxPayload; EnvelopeSize
39	// bytes are reserved, so the inner payload limit is ReliableMaxPayload.
40	//
41	// Delivery guarantees, across disconnects and sender-side restarts:
42	//   - Write side: frames are numbered in write order and streamed
43	//     through a fixed send window. Written frames are journaled in a
44	//     CRC'd replay log; the acknowledged position is recorded in a
45	//     dual-slot checkpoint. After a restart, sending resumes after the
46	//     earliest confirmed position recorded by either file, so an
47	//     acknowledged frame is never counted twice and no frame past it is
48	//     skipped (a resupplied frame is deduped on arrival).
49	//   - Read side: frames are delivered in sequence order exactly once.
50	//     A duplicate of an already delivered or already held frame is
51	//     acknowledged again but delivered once; an in-order gap closed by
52	//     an out-of-order arrival flushes the held run in order; a sequence
53	//     older than the window's duplicate span or more than one window
54	//     width ahead is refused and delivery stops at the current
55	//     position.
56	const (
57		// EnvelopeSize is this layer's per-frame overhead:
58		// 4 (seq) + 4 (ack) + 1 (type) + 2 (flags) + 1 (kind) + 4 (crc32).
59		EnvelopeSize = 16
60	
61		// ReliableMaxPayload is the largest inner payload a reliable data
62		// frame may carry; EnvelopeSize bytes are reserved inside the
63		// underlying frame, whose own limit stays MaxPayload.
64		ReliableMaxPayload = MaxPayload - EnvelopeSize
65	
66		// envelope field offsets.
67		envSeqOff   = 0
68		envAckOff   = 4
69		envTypeOff  = 8
70		envFlagsOff = 9
71		envKindOff  = 11
72		envCRCOff   = 12
73		envBodyOff  = 16
74	)
75	
76	const (
77		envTypeData = 1
78		envTypeAck  = 2
79	
80		// outerKind is the codec-frame Kind of every reliable message; the
81		// caller's Kind travels inside the envelope and is never confused
82		// with this marker.
83		outerKind uint8 = 0xA5
84	)

86	// ErrWindowFull is the established over-limit value a write returns when
87	// the send window already holds the maximum number of unacknowledged
88	// frames. It is the same sentinel the single-frame encoder uses for an
89	// over-limit payload: an over-window write is an over-limit write, and
90	// the offered frame is dropped without entering the window or the log
91	// and without consuming a sequence number.
92	var ErrWindowFull = ErrTooLarge

94	// ReliableFrame is one caller-visible frame on the reliable layer.
95	type ReliableFrame struct {
96		Flags   uint16
97		Kind    uint8
98		Payload []byte
99	}

101	// envelope is one parsed reliable message.
102	type envelope struct {

104		ack     uint32
105		typ     uint8

111	// encodeEnvelope serializes one message into the payload bytes of an
112	// ordinary codec frame.
113	func encodeEnvelope(e envelope) ([]byte, error) {
114		if e.typ == envTypeData && len(e.payload) > ReliableMaxPayload {
115			return nil, ErrTooLarge
116		}
117		out := make([]byte, EnvelopeSize+len(e.payload))
118		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[envSeqOff:envSeqOff+4], e.seq)
119		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[envAckOff:envAckOff+4], e.ack)
120		out[envTypeOff] = e.typ
121		binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(out[envFlagsOff:envFlagsOff+2], e.flags)
122		out[envKindOff] = e.kind
123		copy(out[envBodyOff:], e.payload)
124		h := crc32.NewIEEE()
125		h.Write(out[:envCRCOff])
126		h.Write(out[envBodyOff:])
127		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(out[envCRCOff:envCRCOff+4], h.Sum32())
128		return out, nil

131	// decodeEnvelope parses one message from a codec frame payload. A
132	// damaged envelope is reported with the established checksum value;
133	// nothing is delivered from it.
134	func decodeEnvelope(p []byte) (envelope, error) {
135		var e envelope
136		if len(p) < EnvelopeSize {
137			return e, ErrShortFrame
138		}
139		h := crc32.NewIEEE()
140		h.Write(p[:envCRCOff])
141		h.Write(p[envBodyOff:])
142		if h.Sum32() != binary.BigEndian.Uint32(p[envCRCOff:envCRCOff+4]) {
143			return e, ErrChecksum
144		}
145		e.seq = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(p[envSeqOff : envSeqOff+4])
146		e.ack = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(p[envAckOff : envAckOff+4])
147		e.typ = p[envTypeOff]
148		e.flags = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(p[envFlagsOff : envFlagsOff+2])
149		e.kind = p[envKindOff]
150		body := make([]byte, len(p)-EnvelopeSize)
151		copy(body, p[EnvelopeSize:])
152		e.payload = body
153		return e, nil
154	}

156	// ReliableConfig configures a ReliableSession.
157	type ReliableConfig struct {
158		// Window is the send and receive window width in frames. It must be

167	// ReliableSession is a reliability layer wrapping one Session. Create it
168	// with NewReliable; the wrapped session must not be used directly while
169	// the ReliableSession owns it.

171	// The two directions are independent and may be used concurrently, like
172	// the underlying session. A writer that wants the peer's
173	// acknowledgements to advance its window must let ReadFrame run
174	// (acknowledgements are consumed there, in a dedicated goroutine when
175	// traffic is one-directional).
176	type ReliableSession struct {
177		sess *Session
178		cfg  ReliableConfig
179	
180		wmu sync.Mutex
181		// sendBase is the oldest sequence not yet acknowledged (as a
182		// next-expected ack value); sendNext is the next sequence a newly
183		// written frame gets. Slot i holds sequence sendBase+i while it is
184		// unacknowledged.

186		sendNext uint32
187		window   []windowSlot
188		log      *replayLog

190	
191		rmu sync.Mutex
192		// recvBase is the next sequence due for delivery. It is atomic so the
193		// send paths (Flush, the ack pump) can read the position without
194		// taking rmu: ReadFrame must keep rmu free while blocked in the
195		// underlying reader, otherwise two peers reading at once deadlock.
196		recvBase atomic.Uint32
197		// held parks frames that arrived in-window but ahead of order; it is
198		// guarded by rmu.
199		held map[uint32]ReliableFrame
200		rerr error
201	
202		// ackCh is a coalescing signal: every delivery that moves recvBase
203		// (or repeats a duplicate the sender is still resending) pokes it
204		// non-blockingly, and pumpAck flushes one cumulative acknowledgement
205		// for the latest position. A capacity of 1 is enough because acks
206		// are cumulative. Keeping the write off the read path means two
207		// peers reading at the same time cannot block each other.
208		ackCh  chan struct{}

210		doneCh chan struct{}

219	// NewReliable wraps sess in a reliable session. Write state in
220	// cfg.StateDir is consulted when present: a fresh directory starts at
221	// sequence 0, while a directory left by a crashed or restarted process
222	// resumes from the earliest confirmed position held by its checkpoint
223	// and replay log.
224	//
225	// A checkpoint record torn by a crash mid-write fails its own checksum
226	// and is ignored in favor of the previous complete record. A replayed
227	// log that is truncated or contains a flipped bit fails with
228	// ErrChecksum.
229	func NewReliable(sess *Session, cfg ReliableConfig) (*ReliableSession, error) {
230		if cfg.Window <= 0 {
231			return nil, errors.New("codec: reliable window must be positive")

242			cfg:    cfg,
243			window: make([]windowSlot, cfg.Window),
